nodes.label: Native Webview Architecture
nodes.rationale: Ferx uses native OS webviews to reduce resource overhead relative to Electron-based wrappers while preserving service isolation.

nodes.label: Notification Delivery Separation
nodes.rationale: The injected Notification permission shim only satisfies third-party web app expectations; Ferx shell notifications are separately delivered through the native notification plugin after preference and runtime checks.

nodes.label: Long-Lived Service Webviews
nodes.rationale: Overlay flows park service webviews offscreen rather than close them so authenticated sessions survive and services do not reload when overlays are dismissed.

nodes.label: Serialized Webview Command Queue
nodes.rationale: All page-level webview operations are serialized to prevent service switches, overlay hides, and preload operations from racing.

nodes.label: Frontend Service Module Boundaries
nodes.source_location: Frontend Service Helpers; Where New Logic Should Go
nodes.rationale: Reusable browser-side logic belongs in focused service modules so the top-level Svelte page remains an orchestrator rather than accumulating implementation detail.

nodes.label: Rust Backend Module Boundaries
nodes.source_location: Rust Backend Layout; Where New Logic Should Go
nodes.rationale: The Rust lib module should remain focused on Tauri wiring while service and webview implementation lives in focused sibling modules.

nodes.label: Webview Lifecycle Invariant
nodes.rationale: Service webviews must only close through explicit lifecycle commands; hide operations move them offscreen to preserve sessions and avoid full reloads.

nodes.label: Workspace State Dependency Boundary
nodes.rationale: workspace-state must not import workspace-groups, workspace-groups remains pure, and workspace-actions computes side-effect instructions without invoking Tauri.

nodes.label: Behavioral Test Policy
nodes.rationale: Tests must execute real behavior instead of asserting source strings because textual checks can survive broken behavior and fail on harmless formatting changes.

nodes.label: Generated Tauri Type Freshness Check
nodes.source_location: Verify tauri-commands.ts is up to date

nodes.label: Serialized Cross-Platform Release Builds
nodes.rationale: Release jobs run one at a time because tauri-action merges every platform into the same latest.json asset and concurrent writes could conflict.

nodes.label: Minisign Key Management
nodes.rationale: The private updater key is kept out of Git and stored as GitHub Actions secrets, while the public key is committed for artifact verification.

nodes.label: Publish Latest Updater Manifest
nodes.source_location: Step 8 — Fill in release notes and publish

nodes.label: Private Vulnerability Reporting
nodes.rationale: Potential vulnerabilities must be reported privately so a fix can be coordinated before public disclosure.

nodes.label: Contributor Validation Workflow
nodes.source_location: Checks Before Opening Changes; Working Style
